diagnosis.root_cause: The OLT health check reports overall_status=healthy even though 7 of 8 tested PONs are marked failed. The OLT itself is reachable and SNMP is responsive, so this is a false healthy monitoring result caused by an incorrect health-status aggregation rule. The subscriber's EPON0/7 port is genuinely down: all probed ONUs on that port returned responds=true with online=0.
evidence: The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and the OID subtree, with normal CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime; this rules out an OLT-wide device failure.
The detailed OLT health record marks 7 of 8 tested PONs as failed, leaving only one healthy PON, but overall_status is incorrectly reported as healthy.
The monitoring rules state that an overall healthy label concealing failures on every tested PON or all but one indicates a health-check fault.
The live probe for EPON0/7 returns responds=true and online=0 for every sampled ONU, which is a definite real outage rather than a monitoring silence.
Because all observed ONUs on EPON0/7 are offline, the subscriber's port is down; the VLAN, RADIUS record, router heartbeat, and authentication mapping are otherwise normal.
The customer's optical telemetry before the current dropout was stable and healthy: RX stayed around -21.4 dBm, TX around +2.35 dBm, distance remained 166, and TX bias remained near 11.2 mA.
Session activity is normal at one session in the last 24 hours with a near-normal average duration, so there is no evidence of session flapping or an authentication fault.
The breadth of the failed-port detail makes the service impact OLT-wide, while the fault being reported is the incorrect OLT health status rather than an OLT hardware failure.

remediation.action: Correct the OLT health-check aggregation so an OLT with all or all-but-one PONs failed cannot be reported healthy. Escalate the underlying seven failed PONs, beginning with EPON0/7, for port, splitter, and upstream optical-path investigation and restoration. Re-run live PON probes and verify ONU recovery after repair.

ground_truth.root_cause: The health check marks an OLT critical only when every sampled PON fails. Seven of eight failed here, so it wrote 'healthy' with a null error description while healthy_pons stood at 1 of 8 in the same record. A genuine multi-port outage is running underneath a healthy verdict.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports overall_status healthy with a null error description
The same record holds healthy_pons 1 against total_pons_tested 8, and seven entries in failed_pons_list
The summary label contradicts the detail fields inside one record
The check sets critical only when every sampled PON fails, so seven of eight yields healthy by design
Probing confirms every ONU on EPON0/7 returns responds true with online 0, a definite negative
oid_subtree_responds is true, so this is not the firmware mismatch mechanism
43 of 272 customers on the OLT are offline, far above the 4.85% background rate
Sessions ended together and PON traffic has collapsed from 219 to 6 Mbps
This is a genuine multi-port outage that the health check's status rule conceals

expected_escalation.review_reason: The health check reported healthy during a seven-port outage; the status rule needs correcting

distractors: The health record says healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
A scheduled scan with no complaint gives no reason to look harder
The fault type is a health check defect but the service impact is real
